story: A trial of strength between Vayu and Adisesha is said to have hurled eight pieces of Kailasa southward, one of which became the hill of Thiruengoimalai.

name: Abathsahayeswarar Temple
significance: One of the 275 Paadal Petra Sthalams, at Ponnur in Mayiladuthurai district, celebrated in the Tevaram poetry of Tirugnanasambandar and Tirunavukkarasar.

name: Amravaneswarar Temple
significance: A Paadal Petra Sthalam near Tiruchirappalli glorified by Appar and Sambandar and expanded by 11th-century Chola kings, whose inscriptions line its walls. It is known as a Moola Nakshatra parihara shrine where those born under the Moola star pray for marriage.
story: Shiva is said to have fed a mango to a deer here under the sacred mango tree — maan (deer) giving the village its name Manthurai.

name: Parasunathar Temple
significance: A Shiva temple at Muzhaiyur near the old Chola capital of Pazhayarai, mentioned by the saint Appar and counted among the Vaippu Sthalams of the Tevaram; besides the shivalinga it houses images of Parashurama, Murugan and Vinayaka.

name: Manickavannar Temple
significance: One of the 275 Paadal Petra Sthalams, at Tiruvalaputhur in Mayiladuthurai district, glorified in the early medieval Tevaram poems of Tirugnanasambandar and Sundarar.

name: Kundala Karaneswarar Temple
significance: The 28th Tevara Paadal Petra Sthalam of Chola Nadu north of the Kaveri, near Vaitheeswaran Koil; it is one of the very few shrines where Hanuman is depicted worshipping Shiva.
story: Hanuman is said to have offered his kundalams (earrings) to Shiva here, giving the deity the name Kundala Karaneswarar.

name: Pasupatiswarar Temple
significance: A Paadal Petra Sthalam revered in Sambandar's Tevaram, with 11th-century Chola masonry and inscriptions running from Rajaraja I to Rajaraja III; its white lingam bears the mark of a cow's hoof, and the complex includes a five-tiered rajagopuram and three prakarams.
story: Parvati, cursed to become the cow Kamadhenu for delaying the sunset at play, worshipped Shiva over a snake's lair at Pandanallur until he released her.

name: Palunkanda Nathar Temple
significance: A Shiva temple at Thiruvaipadi near Thiruppanandal, praised by Tirunavukkarasar in the Tevaram and closely tied to the life of Chandeshvara Nayanar, one of the 63 Nayanmars.
story: The cowherd boy Chandesvara raised a shivalinga of sand here and bathed it daily with the milk of his herd, a devotion that won him sainthood.

name: Vilwaneswarar Temple
significance: A Paadal Petra Sthalam north of Kumbakonam on the Kollidam's southern side, revered in the Tevaram by Appar, Sundarar and Sambandar; the temple has a five-tiered gateway tower and the Yama Theertham tank.
story: A hunter chased up a vilva tree on Shivaratri unknowingly showered its leaves on a lingam all night, and the pleased Shiva later saved him from Yama, the god of death.

name: Saptharisheeswarar Temple
significance: A Shiva temple at Lalgudi (Thiruthavathurai) reckoned about 1,200 years old and sung by the saint Appar; it is celebrated for its 30-foot wooden temple chariot bearing over 2,000 carvings, among the tallest in Tamil Nadu.
story: The seven Saptarishis are said to have worshipped Shiva here and, after penance, risen into the sky as the seven stars.

name: Arunajadeswarar (Thaalapureeswarar) Temple
significance: One of the 275 Paadal Petra Sthalams, on the Kollidam at Thiruppanandal, praised by Tirugnanasambandar, Tirunavukkarasar, Nambiyandar Nambi and later Arunagirinathar; the west-facing temple has three prakaras and shrines of Ambika, Durga and Naga Kanni.

name: Ratnagiriswarar Temple
significance: A hill temple in Karur district, one of the 275 Paadal Petra Sthalams, with Tevaram verses composed in its praise by Appar and Sundarar; the shrine crowns the Ratnagiri hill at Ayermalai near Kulithalai.

name: Kadambavaneswarar Temple
significance: One of the 275 Paadal Petra Sthalams, standing on the south bank of the Kaveri at Kulithalai in Karur district, with hymns sung in its praise by Tirunavukkarasar (Appar).
story: Shiva is said to have appeared to the sage Kanva in the kadamba forest here, whence the place was called Kadambanthurai.

name: Tharukavaneswarar (Paraithurainathar) Temple
significance: A Chola-period Paadal Petra Sthalam on the Kaveri west of Tiruchirappalli, honoured in the Tevaram of the Nayanmars; the temple has a seven-tiered gateway tower, two precincts and numerous Chola inscriptions.
story: Shiva as the mendicant Bhikshatana and Vishnu as the enchantress Mohini are said to have humbled the proud sages of the Tharuka forest at this spot.

name: Ujjeevanathar Temple (Uyyakondan Thirumalai)
significance: A Paadal Petra Sthalam on a 30-metre hillock above the Uyyakondan channel in Tiruchirappalli, revered in the Tevaram by Appar, Sambandar and Sundarar. Built in the Sembian Chola age around 950 CE, it bears inscriptions of Rajaraja I and Kulothunga I and was occupied by French and English troops during the 1753–54 siege of Trichinopoly.
story: When Yama came for the sixteen-year-old devotee Markandeya, Shiva burst from the lingam here, kicked Death away and left the boy sixteen forever.

name: Panchavarnaswamy Temple
significance: A Paadal Petra Sthalam in Woraiyur, the ancient Chola capital within present-day Tiruchirappalli, revered in the Tevaram; its lingam is believed to show five different colours through the day, and the temple preserves eight Chola inscriptions naming Rajaraja I and Rajendra I.
story: Shiva is said to have appeared to the sage Udanga in five colours across the day, and five lingams borne by Nagaraja merged into the single image worshipped here.

name: Thayumanaswami Temple, Rockfort
significance: The Shiva temple of Tiruchirappalli's Rockfort, cut into a 273-foot monolith whose cave shrines go back to the Pallavas; the main complex was raised by the Pandyas in the 8th century and renewed by Vijayanagara and Madurai Nayak rulers. The deity is revered in the Tevaram, making it a Paadal Petra Sthalam.
story: Shiva took the form of a devotee's absent mother to deliver Rathnavathi's child during a flood, earning the name Thayumanavar, "he who became a mother".

name: Erumbeeswarar Temple
significance: A Paadal Petra Sthalam crowning a 60-foot hill near Tiruchirappalli, its present form raised by Aditya Chola I after the battle of Tirupurambiyam; the temple preserves 49 Chola inscriptions and draws tens of thousands for the full-moon girivalam circumambulation.
story: Shiva is said to have become an anthill and tilted his head so that ants could climb up and worship him — erumbu, the ant, names the lord Erumbeeswarar.

name: Nedungalanathar Temple
significance: One of the 275 Paadal Petra Sthalams, near Tiruchirappalli, whose presiding deity Nedungalanathar (Nithya Sundareswarar) received ten Tevaram hymns from Tirugnanasambandar.

name: Athmanatheswarar Temple
significance: One of the 275 Paadal Petra Sthalams, at Thiruvalampozhil in Thanjavur district, celebrated in hymns by Tirunavukkarasar; pilgrims come seeking removal of obstacles to marriage and the blessing of children.

name: Pushpavananathar Temple
significance: A Paadal Petra Sthalam near Thiruvaiyaru and one of the Saptha Sthanam temples, revered in the Tevaram; its 9th-century Chola core grew through Vijayanagar and Nayak times, and it is noted for a seated image of Appar and a Durga standing on one leg.
story: Indra, cursed by Gautama with a thousand marks, is said to have been cleansed after worshipping here with flowers — poo — which named the lord Pushpavananathar.

name: Brahma Sira Kandeeswarar Temple
significance: A Paadal Petra Sthalam near Thiruvaiyaru revered in the Tevaram and counted among the eight Ashta Veeratanam temples marking Shiva's heroic deeds — here the severing of Brahma's fifth head; unusually, the complex contains a separate shrine to Brahma. Inscriptions record Chola, Thanjavur Nayak and Maratha patronage.
story: Shiva plucked off Brahma's fifth head at this place and was himself freed of the resulting sin after bathing in the temple's Kamala Pushkarani tank.

name: Odhanavaneswarar Temple
significance: A Paadal Petra Sthalam in Thanjavur district revered by Sambandar, Appar and Sundarar, known as Dakshina Kailasham; its 9th-century Chola masonry was extended to the 16th century with four gopurams and three precincts, with Pandya and Maratha contributions on record.
story: Shiva is said to have granted a devotee an inexhaustible vessel of food here, making the place Chotruthurai — "the refuge of rice".

name: Vedapuriswarar Temple
significance: An early Chola Paadal Petra Sthalam near Thiruvaiyaru revered by Appar and Sambandar, and one of the Saptha Sthanam temples; on set days in the month of Panguni the sun's rays fall directly on the lingam.
story: The lord is called Vazhaimadunathar because the lingam is said to have emerged from a banana tree.

name: Vasishteswarar Temple
significance: A Chola-built Paadal Petra Sthalam at Thenkudithittai near Thanjavur, hymned by Sambandar and Appar; a Chandrakanta stone in the vimana drips water on the lingam every 24 minutes, and the temple is a noted shrine of Guru (Brihaspati), who stands in a separate sanctum.
story: After the great deluge only this mound stayed above water, where Brahma and Vishnu found a lingam and worshipped it until Shiva appeared and restored their offices.

name: Alandurainathar Temple
significance: The Paadal Petra Sthalam of Pullamangai near Thanjavur, glorified by Tirugnanasambandar and counted by art historians among the four earliest surviving temples of the Chola Empire; it is celebrated for exquisite sculpture, including miniature panels narrating the Ramayana.

name: Chakravageswarar Temple
significance: A Paadal Petra Sthalam on the Kudamurutti branch of the Kaveri near Ayyampettai, honoured in Thevaram verses by Appar and Sambandar; begun under Aditya I and enlarged by 11th-century Cholas, it keeps inscriptions of Rajaraja I and Rajendra I and a rare circular two-tiered vimana. It is also counted among the seven Saptamatrika shrines.
story: Vishnu is said to have received his discus, the chakra, after worshipping at this temple, an event remembered in the village's name.

name: Mullaivananathar Temple (Garbharakshambigai)
significance: Shiva shrine on the Kaveri attributed to the Early Chola king Killivalavan, counted among the 275 Paadal Petra Sthalams hymned by Tirugnanasambandar. Its goddess Garbharakshambigai draws devotees seeking safe pregnancy and childbirth.
story: The goddess is believed to have received her initiation at this shrine.

name: Palaivananathar Temple
significance: One of the 275 Paadal Petra Sthalams praised in the 7th-century Tevaram, at Papanasam in the Kaveri delta. The Chola-founded complex was rebuilt in masonry under 16th-century Vijayanagar rule, with a granary added by Raghunatha Nayak, and carries inscriptions of Kulothunga Chola I and III.
story: Shiva is said to have absolved the sins of Vishnu, Brahma, Rama and Sita here, earning the name Papanasanathar, the destroyer of sins.

name: Kalyanasundaresar Temple
significance: A 9th-century Chola perunkoil on an elevated platform near Kumbakonam, revered in the 7th-century Tevaram as a Paadal Petra Sthalam. Inscriptions of Uttama Chola and Raja Raja Chola survive, and Vijayanagar dynasties later expanded it.
story: Sage Agastya is said to have witnessed the wedding of Shiva and Parvati at this spot and installed a lingam here.

name: Pasupatheeswarar Temple
significance: An elevated maadakoil counted among the 70 temples attributed to the 7th-century king Kochengat Chola, with its present masonry from the 9th-century Cholas and Nayak-era expansions. A Paadal Petra Sthalam sung by Sambandar, noted for its rare set of five Bhairava images.
story: The celestial cow Kamadhenu is said to have worshipped Shiva here to be freed from sage Vasishtha's curse.

name: Sakthivanesvara Temple
significance: A Paadal Petra Sthalam near Patteeswaram whose lingam bears the mark of Parvati's embrace, glorified in the Tevaram hymns. Devotees pray here to be blessed with the life partner of their choice.
story: Parvati is said to have done penance here and embraced Shiva when he appeared as a column of fire, giving the place its name Sakthimutram.

name: Thenupuriswarar Temple
significance: A Paadal Petra Sthalam near Kumbakonam revered in the 7th-century Tevaram, founded under the Cholas and given its present masonry form by the 16th-century Nayaks.
story: When Sambandar arrived in scorching heat, Shiva sent attendants with a pearl canopy and ordered Nandi to move aside so the saint could see the sanctum from outside.

name: Pazhayarai Vadathali Temple
significance: The northern shrine of Pazhayarai, a capital region of the Chola empire near Kumbakonam, with inscriptions from the 8th-9th centuries and a Later Chola gopuram. It is revered as a Paadal Petra Sthalam in the Tevaram.
story: The moon god is said to have worshipped Shiva at this spot, prompting the lord's appearance.

name: Kabartheeswarar Temple
significance: One of the largest temple complexes in Tamil Nadu, with a seven-tiered gopuram and three precincts, built up from Chola-era masonry with Thanjavur Nayak expansions. It is a Paadal Petra Sthalam glorified in the 7th-century Tevaram.
story: The sage Herandar is said to have travelled underground to bring the Kaveri to earth, making the river swirl around this place - hence the name Thiruvalanchuzhi.

name: Adi Kumbeswarar Temple
significance: The principal Shiva temple of Kumbakonam, founded by the 9th-century Cholas and enlarged by the Thanjavur Nayaks, spread over three concentric compounds with four gopurams. A Paadal Petra Sthalam and one of the twelve temples tied to the Mahamaham festival held every twelve years.
story: The town's name is traced to Brahma's pot of creation-seeds, which Shiva's arrow displaced so that nectar fell at this spot.

name: Nageswaraswamy Temple (Kudanthai Keezhkottam)
deity: Shiva (Nageswarar, lord of the serpent king), consort Periyanayagi
significance: Reckoned among the earliest of all Chola temples, raised in the 9th century under Aditya Chola in Kumbakonam. It is a Paadal Petra Sthalam revered by the Nayanars in the Tevaram.
story: During Rajendra Chola's Ganges expedition the army is said to have brought back a beautiful Vinayagar image, installed here as Gangai Vinayagar.

name: Kasi Viswanathar Temple (Kudanthai Karonam)
significance: A Paadal Petra Sthalam of Kumbakonam revered in the 7th-century Tevaram, rebuilt in the 16th century during the Nayak period. It is one of the twelve Shiva temples connected with the Mahamaham festival.
story: Rama and Lakshmana are said to have worshipped Shiva here while searching for Sita, obtaining Rudramsam to fight Ravana.

name: Naganathar Temple
significance: A Chola-built Paadal Petra Sthalam near Kumbakonam, famous as the Rahu shrine among the Navagraha temples of the Kaveri delta. The presiding Naganathar is revered in the 7th-century Tevaram.
story: Serpent deities led by Adishesha are said to have done penance here and won Shiva's grace, giving the lord his name Naganathar.

name: Mahalingeswarar Temple
significance: One of the great Shaiva temples of the Kaveri delta, its oldest masonry from the 9th-century Cholas with four gopurams and three precincts expanded under the Thanjavur Nayaks. A Paadal Petra Sthalam counted among the foremost shrines of Saivism.
story: A Chola prince pursued by a Brahmin's vengeful spirit is said to have entered the temple, prayed to Shiva, and escaped through another gate - a circuit worshippers still repeat.

name: Abathsahayeswarar Temple (Then Kurangaduthurai)
significance: The Then Kurangaduthurai shrine at Aduthurai, one of the 275 Paadal Petra Sthalams of the Tevaram, founded by the Cholas and rebuilt in masonry during the 16th-century Nayak period.
story: Sugriva, fleeing his brother Vali, is said to have prayed to Shiva here and been rescued when the lord turned him into a swan.

name: Umamaheswarar Temple
significance: The Tirunallam shrine of the Tevaram, rebuilt in the 10th century by the Chola queen Sembiyan Mahadevi over an earlier foundation. It is noted for the paintings of its front mandapa and the miniature sculptures outside the sanctum.

name: Kokileswarar Temple
significance: A Kaveri-bank Paadal Petra Sthalam glorified by the Tamil Saivite saints in the early medieval Tevaram poems.
story: A devotee named Chandan, cursed by Indra to be reborn as a nightingale (kokila), is said to have regained human form by meditating on Shiva here.

name: Masilamaniswara Temple
significance: A 9th-century Chola temple at Thiruvaduthurai on the Kaveri, expanded by later Chola rulers and rich in inscriptions from the reigns of Parantaka I and Rajaraja I. It is one of the 275 Paadal Petra Sthalams of the Tevaram canon.
story: The saint Tirumular is said to have entered the body of the dead herdsman Moolan here to console his grieving cattle, and remained in that form for good.

name: Ukthavedeeswarar Temple
significance: A Kaveri-bank shrine celebrated by Sambandar in the Tevaram, held in tradition to be the venue of Shiva's wedding to Parvati.
story: After the wedding held here, Shiva is said to have left his sandals behind before setting out for Mount Kailash.

name: Vedapureeswarar Temple
significance: A Kaveri-bank Paadal Petra Sthalam at Therazhundur glorified by Tirugnanasambandar in the Tevaram, bearing Imperial Chola inscriptions dated to the reign of Kulottunga Chola I.

name: Mayuranathaswami Temple
significance: The great temple of Mayiladuthurai, attested in the 7th-century hymns of Appar and Sambandar and renovated by queen Sembiyan Mahadevi in the 10th century. It ranks among the six Kaveri shrines held equal to Kashi Vishwanath of Varanasi.
story: Parvati, cursed to become a peahen, is said to have worshipped Shiva here and regained her form as Abhayambika - giving the town its name, Mayiladuthurai.

name: Uchiravaneswarar Temple
deity: Shiva (Uchira Vaneswarar), consort Veyuru Tholi Ammai
significance: One of the 275 Paadal Petra Sthalams, glorified in the medieval Tevaram hymns of Tirugnanasambandar at Vilanagar near Mayiladuthurai.

name: Veerateswarar Temple
significance: One of the eight Ashta Veeratta sthalams marking Shiva's heroic deeds - here the destruction of Daksha's sacrifice - built by the 9th-century Cholas and expanded by the Thanjavur Nayaks. It is a Paadal Petra Sthalam of the Tevaram canon.
story: Shiva is said to have destroyed Daksha for insulting Dakshayani at his sacrifice, then restored him to life with a goat's head.

name: Swarnapureeswarar Temple
significance: The Tiruchemponpalli shrine on the Kaveri, a Paadal Petra Sthalam glorified by both Sambandar and Tirunavukkarasar in the Tevaram.

name: Natrunaiyappar Temple
deity: Shiva (Natrunaiyappar), consorts Malaiyaan Madanthai and Parvatha Putthiri
significance: The Tirunanipalli shrine of the Tevaram, built by Parantaka Chola I in the 10th century, whose unusually large sanctum is said to have once admitted elephants for worship.
story: Shiva is believed to have granted wedding darshan here to Vinayaka and the sage Agastya.

name: Valampurinathar Temple
significance: The Tiruvalampuram shrine near the Kaveri's mouth, raised in the medieval Chola period and revered as a Paadal Petra Sthalam in the 7th-century Tevaram hymns.

name: Sankaranyeswarar Temple
deity: Shiva (Sankaranyeswarar, as Somaskandar), consort Soundara Nayaki
significance: A conch-shaped shrine at Thalaichangadu attributed to the Early Chola king Kochengannan and renovated over later centuries, praised by Sambandar in the Tevaram.
story: Vishnu is believed to have worshipped Shiva at this place.

name: Thanthondreeswarar Temple
significance: The self-manifested Shiva shrine of Aakkur, one of the 275 Paadal Petra Sthalams glorified by the Nayanars in the early medieval Tevaram.
story: An ailing Chola king fed a thousand guests for 48 days; Shiva is said to have come as the thousandth and cured him, after which the temple rose here.

name: Amritaghateswarar-Abirami Temple
significance: The celebrated shrine where Shiva is held to have conquered death itself, saving the boy-sage Markandeya from Yama - hence his name Kala-samhara. A 9th-century Chola foundation expanded by the Thanjavur Nayaks, and a Paadal Petra Sthalam of the Tevaram.
story: When Yama came for the sixteen-year-old devotee Markandeya, Shiva burst from the lingam and subdued death, granting the boy eternal youth.

name: Brahmapureeswarar Temple
significance: The Tirukkadavur Mayanam shrine beside Thirukkadaiyur, one of the five sacred Mayana (cremation-ground) kshetras where Shiva is held to have burnt Brahma to ashes. A Paadal Petra Sthalam with Chola-era idols and Vijayanagar-period inscriptions.
story: At the end of every eon Shiva burns Brahma to ashes, and the celestials pleaded here for Brahma's restoration so creation could continue.

name: Sundareshwarar Temple
significance: A Paadal Petra Sthalam in the Karaikal district of Puducherry, glorified by Tirugnanasambandar in the early medieval Tevaram poems.

name: Parvatheeswarar Temple
significance: The Tiruttelicheri shrine, in the village now called Koilpathu on the periphery of Karaikal, one of the 275 Paadal Petra Sthalams sung by Tirugnanasambandar in the Tevaram.

name: Yazhmoorinathar Temple
significance: The Dharmapuram shrine near Karaikal in the Union Territory of Puducherry, one of the 275 Paadal Petra Sthalams glorified by Tirugnanasambandar in the Tevaram; its deity's name recalls the bending of the yazh, the ancient Tamil lute.

name: Dharbaranyeswarar Temple (Thirunallar Saniswaran Temple)
deity: Shiva (Dharbaranyeswarar), consort Praneswari Amman; shrine of Shani (Saturn)
significance: The most famous Shani shrine among the nine Navagraha temples of the Kaveri delta, where Saturn's image stands within a Paadal Petra Sthalam of Shiva. The present masonry is 9th-century Chola work with Vijayanagar-era expansions.
story: When a corrupt headman threatened a shepherd who supplied milk for the lord's ablutions, Shiva is said to have intervened with his trident to stop the king's punishment.

name: Iravatheeswarar Temple
significance: A roughly thousand-year-old Medieval Chola shrine at Tirukkottaru, whose Tevaram praise by Sambandar is inscribed within the sanctum itself.
story: Indra's elephant Airavata, cursed by the sage Durvasa, is said to have worshipped here among the holy places that freed him after a hundred years.

name: Mahakalanathar Temple
significance: The Ambar Maakaalam shrine, one of the 275 Paadal Petra Sthalams glorified by Tirugnanasambandar in the early medieval Tevaram poems.

name: Meganathar Temple
significance: A Paadal Petra Sthalam of the Tevaram, renowned for its shrine of Lalithambika: tradition holds that the Lalita Sahasranama was composed here and taught to Agastya by Hayagriva.
story: Garuda and Aruna, mounts of Vishnu and Surya, are said to have been born here to Vinata and Kadru after the sisters worshipped Shiva.

name: Sakalabhuvaneswarar Temple (Ilamkovil)
significance: The Ilamkovil or younger shrine within the Tirumeeyachur temple precinct, counted separately among the 275 Paadal Petra Sthalams and glorified by Tirunavukkarasar in the Tevaram.

name: Muktheeswarar Temple
significance: The Thilataipati (Thilatharpanapuri) shrine at Sethalapathy in Tiruvarur district, one of the 275 Paadal Petra Sthalams celebrated by Tirugnanasambandar in the Tevaram.

name: Paampuranathar Temple
significance: A Paadal Petra Sthalam of the Tevaram canon where devotees especially seek relief from Rahu-Ketu and serpent doshas, and pray against childlessness.

name: Sukshmapureeswarar Temple
significance: The Sirukudi shrine in Tiruvarur district, one of the 275 Paadal Petra Sthalams glorified by Tirugnanasambandar in the early medieval Tevaram poems.

name: Veezhinathar Temple
significance: The 61st Paadal Petra shrine of Chola Nadu south of the Kaveri, in Kudavasal taluk of Tiruvarur district, where Parvati reborn as Katyayani is held to have wed Shiva.
story: The saint Mizhalai Kurumbar offered vila fruit to Shiva each day and was rewarded with the lord's darshan.

name: Agnipureeswarar Temple
significance: The Tiruvanniyur shrine in the Kaveri delta, one of the 275 Paadal Petra Sthalams, glorified by the Nayanar Tirunavukkarasar in the Tevaram.

name: Sarguneswarar Temple
significance: The Karuvili Kottittai shrine of the Tevaram canon in Tiruvarur district, where worship is believed to grant salvation and release from rebirth.

name: Sivanandeswarar Temple
significance: The Penu Perunturai shrine near Kumbakonam, one of the 275 Paadal Petra Sthalams glorified by Tirugnanasambandar in the early medieval Tevaram poems.

name: Siddhanatheswarar Temple
significance: The Naraiyur shrine in present-day Nachiyar Koil near Kumbakonam, one of the 275 Paadal Petra Sthalams glorified in the early medieval Tevaram poems.

name: Padikasu Nathar Temple
significance: One of the 275 Paadal Petra Sthalams praised in the Tevaram hymns, with a 9th-century Chola masonry structure later expanded by the Thanjavur Nayaks. The village is remembered as the birthplace of Pugalthunai Nayanar, one of the 63 Nayanmars.
story: Shiva is said to have left a gold coin (padikasu) each day for the poor devotee Pugazh Thunai who kept serving the deity through a famine.

name: Sivagurunathaswamy Temple
significance: A Paadal Petra Sthalam mentioned in the 7th-century Tevaram canon, originally raised by the Cholas with the present masonry structure built under the 16th-century Nayaks. Sivapuram village near Kumbakonam is known chiefly for this shrine.
story: Tradition holds that Surya, Chandra, Brahma and Vishnu in his boar form all worshipped the deity at this site.

name: Sarguna Lingeswarar Temple
deity: Shiva as Sarguna Lingeswarar (sand Prithvi linga)
significance: Also known as Karukudi Nathar Temple, this shrine near Kumbakonam was sung by the saint Sambandar in the Tevaram; its main icon is a shivalinga of sand. Pilgrims traditionally seek relief here from skin ailments.
story: A trader named Dhananjayan is said to have been cured of leprosy at this place.

name: Vanchinadha Swamy Temple
significance: One of the 275 Paadal Petra Sthalams revered in the Tevaram, with an 11th-century Chola masonry structure expanded by the Thanjavur Nayaks in the 16th century.
story: Shiva is said to have appeared as Vanchinathar at the village border to halt Yama when the god of death pursued a sage doing penance here.

name: Madhuvaneswarar Temple
significance: A Paadal Petra Sthalam in Nannilam town praised by the saint Sambandar in the Tevaram; its construction is traditionally attributed to the Early Chola king Kocengannan.
story: The temple town's name is traced to a forest of madhu trees believed to have once covered the region.

name: Soundareswararswamy Temple
significance: One of the 275 Paadal Petra Sthalams, centred on a sacred palmyra tree and associated with the Early Chola king Karikala.
story: Karikala is said to have been standing under the temple's palmyra tree when the royal elephant identified him as king, leading to his coronation.

name: Veerateeswarar Temple, Thiruvirkudi
significance: A Paadal Petra Sthalam sung by Sambandar and one of the eight Ashta Veeratta Sthalams marking Shiva's victories over demons; the present masonry structure dates to the 9th-century Cholas with Nayak-era expansions.
story: Shiva is said to have manifested here as Veerateeswarar to destroy the demon Jalandhara, who had been born of the fire of Shiva's third eye cast into the ocean.

name: Vardhamaneswarar Temple (Tiruppugalur Vardhamaneeswaram)
deity: Shiva as Vardhamaneswarar / Konal Piran (consort Karunthazhkuzhali)
significance: Counted separately among the 275 Paadal Petra Sthalams though it shares its precinct with the Agnipureeswarar temple of Tiruppugalur; it was praised by Sambandar. Its linga is known as the Konal (skewed) lingam for its tilted form.

name: Ramanathaswami Temple (Ramanadeeswaram)
significance: One of the 275 Paadal Petra Sthalams, located between Tiruvarur and Mayiladuthurai and linked in tradition with Rama's worship of Shiva.
story: Rama is believed to have worshipped Shiva here, as at Rameswaram, to absolve himself of the sin of killing Ravana.

name: Tirupayatrunathar Temple
significance: One of the 275 Paadal Petra Sthalams, glorified in the Tevaram verses of the saint Tirunavukkarasar (Appar).

name: Uthirapasupatheeswarar Temple
deity: Shiva as Uthirapasupatheeswarar (consort Vaaitha Tirukuzhal Umai Nayaki)
significance: One of the 275 Paadal Petra Sthalams, sung by both Sambandar and Tirunavukkarasar; the place was historically known as Ganapatheesaram.

name: Rathnagiriswarar Temple
significance: One of the 275 Paadal Petra Sthalams, its glories sung by the saints Appar and Tirugnana Sambandar.
story: The village is said to take its name from a marugal plantain growing since time immemorial on the northern side of the temple.

name: Ayavandeeswarar Temple
significance: One of the 275 Paadal Petra Sthalams glorified by Tirugnanasambandar in the Tevaram, and also counted among the Vaippu Sthalams mentioned by Appar.

name: Kayarohanaswami Temple
significance: A Paadal Petra Sthalam in existence since the 6th century CE and rebuilt by the Pallavas, Cholas and Vijayanagara kings; it is linked to the Lakulisha tradition and houses a Thyagaraja image of lapis lazuli.
story: A Chola king, Mucukunta, is said to have won seven Thyagaraja images from Indra, installed across the Cauvery delta as the Saptha Vidangam shrines whose deities dance in procession.

name: Sikkal Navaneetheswarar Temple
significance: One of the 275 Paadal Petra Sthalams glorified by Tirugnanasambandar; the complex also holds the well-known Singaravelan (Murugan) shrine.

name: Keezhvelur Kediliappar Temple
significance: One of the 275 Paadal Petra Sthalams glorified in the Tevaram; its sculptures and mentions in old Saiva literature are held to show an age of a thousand years or more.

name: Deva Pureeswarar Temple
significance: One of the 275 Paadal Petra Sthalams, traditionally visited by the unmarried and by couples praying for children.
story: Kubera is said to have worshipped Shiva here to recover wealth stolen by Ravana, and the Devas to be absolved of slaying Vruddhasura.

name: Tirunethranathar Temple
significance: One of the 275 Paadal Petra Sthalams, celebrated in the Tevaram verses of the saint Tirunavukkarasar.

name: Araneri Achaleswarar Temple
significance: A shrine within the precincts of the great Thyagaraja temple of Tiruvarur that is counted separately among the 275 Paadal Petra Sthalams, glorified by the saint Tirunavukkarasar.

name: Thyagaraja Temple, Tiruvarur
deity: Shiva as Thyagarajaswami / Putridankondar (consorts Neelotpalambika and Kamalambika)
significance: One of India's largest temple complexes at 8.1 hectares with nine gopurams and Asia's heaviest processional chariot, and a Paadal Petra Sthalam revered in the Tevaram. Believed to have been initiated by the Pallavas in the 7th century, the present masonry structure was built by the 9th-century Cholas, and it heads the seven Saptha Vidangam shrines.
story: King Muchukunda is said to have won from Indra the image of Shiva dancing on Vishnu's chest by correctly choosing it among seven identical icons.

name: Thoovanayanar Thoovainathar Temple (Paravai Un Mandali)
significance: A shrine on Tiruvarur's East Street, historically called Arurparavaiyunmandazhi, counted among the 275 Paadal Petra Sthalams and glorified by Tirugnanasambandar.

name: Vilamal Pathanchali Manoharar Temple
deity: Shiva as Pathanchali Manoharar (consort Yazhinum Menmozhiyaal)
significance: One of the 275 Paadal Petra Sthalams, glorified in the Tevaram verses of Tirugnanasambandar.

name: Karavera Nathar Temple
significance: One of the 275 Paadal Petra Sthalams with hymns by the Tevaram poet-saints; unmarried women traditionally visit seeking blessings for marriage.

name: Tirupperuvelur Abhimuktheeswarar Temple
significance: One of the 275 Paadal Petra Sthalams, glorified in the Tevaram by both Tirugnanasambandar and Tirunavukkarasar; the site is also known as Tirupperuvelur.

name: Nardana Pureeswarar Temple
significance: A Paadal Petra Sthalam praised by the saint Tirunavukkarasar; prayer here is traditionally believed to cure leprosy.
story: The Pandya king Nedunchezhiyan is believed to have defeated the Chera and Chola kings at this place.

name: Koneswarar Temple, Kudavasal
significance: One of the 275 Paadal Petra Sthalams glorified by Tirugnanasambandar, built as an elevated maadakkovil attributed to the Early Chola king Kochengat Chola before 660 CE; it has an 80-foot rajagopuram and two prakarams.
story: During the great deluge, the lid of Brahma's pot holding the seeds of all living beings is said to have come to rest at this spot.

name: Tirucherai Gnanaparameswarar Temple
significance: One of the 275 Paadal Petra Sthalams, where the Nayanmars Appar and Sambandar sang in praise of the deity.
story: The sage Markandeya, the river-goddess Kaveri and the rishi Dowmya are said to have worshipped Shiva at this shrine.

name: Apatsahayesvarar Temple, Alangudi
deity: Shiva as Apathsahyesvarar (consort Elavarkuzhali); Guru (Jupiter) shrine
significance: A Paadal Petra Sthalam revered in the Tevaram and one of Tamil Nadu's nine Navagraha pilgrimage temples, honoured as the Guru (Jupiter) sthalam. The original complex is credited to the Cholas, with the present masonry built under the 16th-century Nayaks.
story: Shiva is said to have drunk the deadly poison of the ocean-churning here, earning the name Apatsahayesvarar, the saviour in peril.

name: Aridwaramangalam Padaleswarar Temple
significance: One of the 275 Paadal Petra Sthalams glorified by Tirugnanasambandar, and one of the five Pancha Aranya (forest) Sthalams of the Kumbakonam-Tiruvarur region.
story: Shiva is said to have hidden underground before his wedding, and Vishnu, as a boar, dug a doorway to find him, giving the place the name Haridwara, Hari's door.

name: Avalivanallur Satchinathar Temple
significance: One of the 275 Paadal Petra Sthalams glorified in the Tevaram, and part of the Pancha Aranya (five forest) Sthalams cluster of the Kumbakonam-Tiruvarur region.

name: Paridiniyamam Parithiappar Temple
significance: One of the Paadal Petra Sthalams glorified by Tirugnanasambandar; the temple marks the spot where the sun god is believed to have worshipped Shiva, giving the place its name.
story: Surya, the sun god, is said to have worshipped Shiva at this site.

name: Venni Karumbeswarar Temple
significance: One of the 275 Paadal Petra Sthalams glorified in the Tevaram; devotees traditionally offer sugar to the deity seeking a cure for diabetes.
story: The main linga is shaped like a bundle of sugarcane stems tied together, karumbu being Tamil for sugarcane.

name: Chathuranga Vallabhanathar Temple
significance: One of the 275 Paadal Petra Sthalams, praised by Sambandar; the temple is traditionally frequented by asthma patients seeking relief.
story: A childless king, Vasudevan, lost a game of chess to Shiva disguised as a siddha, after which Parvati was born to him as the princess Rajarajeswari.

name: Parijatha Vaneswarar Temple
deity: Shiva as Parijatha Vaneswarar / Kalarmulainathar (consort Amudhavalli)
significance: One of the 275 Paadal Petra Sthalams with Tevaram hymns by Sambandar and Tirunavukkarasar, marked by an 80-foot five-tiered east-facing rajagopuram.
story: The sage Durvasa is said to have brought parijatha flowers from the celestial world and installed a shivalinga beneath a parijatha tree in the grove he planted here.

name: Ponvaithanathar Temple
significance: One of the 275 Paadal Petra Sthalams, celebrated in the Tevaram hymns of the saints Appar and Sundarar.

name: Tiruvusaattaanam Mandirapureeswarar Temple
significance: One of the 275 Paadal Petra Sthalams, glorified in the Tevaram verses of Tirugnanasambandar.

name: Sarguna Nathar Temple
significance: One of the 275 Paadal Petra Sthalams with hymns by Sambandar, traditionally visited by devotees seeking freedom from the fear of death.
story: Yama, the god of death, is said to have worshipped Shiva here to atone for trying to carry off the sage Markandeya.

name: Karpaganatharkulam Karpaganathar Temple
significance: One of the 275 Paadal Petra Sthalams glorified by Tirugnanasambandar; its main shivalinga is unusual for its hexagonal shape.

name: Kottur Kozhundeeswarar Temple
significance: One of the 275 Paadal Petra Sthalams glorified by Tirugnanasambandar; the place was historically known as Indirapuram.

name: Vandurai Nathar Temple
deity: Shiva as Vandurai Nathar (consort Vel Nedunganni)
significance: One of the 275 Paadal Petra Sthalams, with Tevaram hymns composed by the saint Sambandar.
story: The sage Brungi, cursed by Parvati for honouring only Shiva, is said to have become a bee and entered the deity's idol here.

name: Tirukkollampudur Vilvaranyeswarar Temple
significance: One of the 275 Paadal Petra Sthalams glorified by Tirugnanasambandar, and one of the five Pancha Aranya (forest) Sthalams, associated with the vilva grove.

name: Pereyil Jagadeeswarar Temple
significance: One of the 275 Paadal Petra Sthalams, celebrated in the Tevaram by the saint Tirunavukkarasar; the site's historical name is Pereyil, and the shrine stands in Tirukkollampudur village.

name: Tirukkollikkadu Agneeswarar Temple
deity: Shiva as Agneeswarar (consort Panjin Melladi Ammai)
significance: The 115th of the 275 Paadal Petra Sthalams, glorified by Tirugnanasambandar; worship here is believed to burn away obstacles and bring good fortune.

name: Thiruthangur Vellimalainathar Temple
significance: One of the 275 Paadal Petra Sthalams, glorified in the Tevaram verses of Tirugnanasambandar.

name: Tirunellikka Nellivananathar Temple
significance: One of the 275 Paadal Petra Sthalams, glorified in the Tevaram verses of Tirugnanasambandar.

name: Kannayariamudayar Temple, Thirukkarayil
deity: Shiva as Kannayiranathar, with Parvati as Kailasanayaki
significance: A medieval Chola-period Shiva temple of the Tiruvarur delta country, counted among the Paadal Petra Sthalams hymned in the Tevaram. Devotees seek the deity here for relief from planetary afflictions.
story: Brahma is said to have raised a sand linga here to be freed of the curse he earned by falsely claiming to have found the crown of Shiva's cosmic flame.

name: Nadutariappar Temple, Kanrappur
deity: Shiva as Nadutariappar, with Parvati as Srivalli Nayagi
significance: An 11th-century Chola temple near Tiruvarur with a five-tiered rajagopuram, honoured in the Tevaram hymns of Appar and counted among the 275 Paadal Petra Sthalams.
story: A Shaiva woman whose husband smashed her linga worshipped a carpenter's wedge instead; when he swung an axe at it, Shiva manifested from the wedge, giving the deity his name.

name: Manathunainathar Temple, Valivalam
deity: Shiva as Manathunainathar, with Parvati as Maazhai Onkanni
builtDisplay: by 7th c. (attr. Early Chola king Kocengannan); renovated later
significance: One of the 275 Paadal Petra Sthalams, glorified in Tevaram hymns by Sambandar, Appar and Sundarar, and traditionally attributed to the Early Chola king Kocengannan. It is classed as a Madakkoil, built raised so that an elephant cannot climb its steps.

name: Kaichineswarar Temple, Kaichinam
deity: Shiva as Kaichineswarar, with Parvati as Palvalai Nayaki
significance: A village Shiva shrine of the Tiruvarur district counted among the 275 Paadal Petra Sthalams, glorified in the early medieval Tevaram hymns of Sambandar.

name: Vaimoornathar Temple, Tiruvaimur
significance: Paadal Petra Sthalam no. 124, a Shiva shrine revered in the 7th-century hymns of the saints Appar and Sambandar.
story: Tradition holds that the Chola king Mucukunta, choosing rightly among seven identical Thyagaraja images given by Indra, had one of the remaining six installed at Thiruvaimur.

name: Vedaranyeswarar Temple
builtDisplay: by early 7th c.; structural temple credited to Aditya Chola (871-907)
significance: The great Shiva temple of Vedaranyam, the ancient Tirumaraikkadu ('forest of the Vedas'), and the only shrine mentioned in all seven Thirumurais of the Tamil Saiva canon. Chola kings from Rajaraja I onward endowed it richly.
story: Its doors, sealed since the Vedas themselves worshipped here, are said to have been sung open by Appar and closed again by Sambandar's hymn.

name: Agastheeswarar Temple, Agasthiyampalli
deity: Shiva as Agastheeswarar, with Parvati as Pakampiriyal Nayagi
builtDisplay: Medieval Chola; Pandya and Nayak additions
significance: A medieval Chola granite temple near Vedaranyam bearing grant inscriptions of Rajaraja I, Rajendra I and Kulothunga I, revered in the Tevaram and classed a Paadal Petra Sthalam.
story: When the earth tilted at Shiva's wedding, sage Agastya was sent south to restore the balance, and Shiva appeared to him here in his marriage form.

name: Kodi Kuzhagar Temple
deity: Shiva as Kuzhagar, with Thadangani Amman
builtDisplay: 9th c. (Chola); inscriptions from Aditya I onward
significance: The land's-end Shiva shrine of Kodikkarai at Point Calimere, a Paadal Petra Sthalam of the Tevaram canon carrying Chola inscriptions from Aditya I, Rajaraja I, Rajendra I and Kulothunga I.

name: Aappudaiyar Temple, Thiru Aappanoor
significance: A Paadal Petra Sthalam within Madurai city, first raised by Pandya kings and later expanded under the Nayaks and Sethupathis, with a Somaskanda image of note.
story: A carpenter's wedge ('aappu') is said to have turned into a Shivalinga so the Pandya king Solandhagan could cross the flooded Vaigai, naming both temple and deity.

name: Subramaniya Swamy Temple, Thiruparankundram
deity: Murugan (Subramaniya); Shiva as Parangirinathar within the complex
significance: One of the Six Abodes of Murugan, carved into the Thiruparankundram hillock by the Pandyas in the 6th century, with the Shiva shrine of Parangirinathar making it a Paadal Petra Sthalam as well. Nayak-era pillared halls front the ancient cave sanctum.
story: After slaying the asura Surapadman at Tiruchendur, Murugan is said to have married Indra's daughter Deivanai here.

name: Edaganathar Temple
deity: Shiva as Edaganathar, with Parvati as Elavaarkuzhali (Visalakshi)
significance: A Shiva temple on the Vaigai bank northwest of Madurai, founded under the Pandyas with its present masonry raised in the Nayak period, and hymned by Sambandar among the Paadal Petra Sthalams.
story: In Sambandar's contest with the Jains, his palm-leaf hymn floated upstream against the Vaigai and landed here, giving Thiruvedagam its name.

name: Kodunkundreeswarar Temple, Piranmalai
deity: Shiva as Kodunkundra Nathar, with Parvati as Thenammal
builtDisplay: by 7th c. (Tevaram era); Marudu-brother additions 18th c.
significance: A hill temple rising in three tiers over Piranmalai, sung by Sambandar among the Paadal Petra Sthalams; the Marudu brothers of Sivaganga were among its later patrons.
story: Piranmalai itself is said to be a block of Mount Meru blown off during the contest between the serpent king Adisesha and the wind god Vayu.

name: Tiruttalinathar Temple, Tiruppattur
deity: Shiva as Tiruttalinathar, with Parvati as Sivakami (Soundarya Nayaki)
builtDisplay: by 7th c. (Tevaram era); patronage from Chola, Pandya and later rulers
significance: Regarded as the sixth of the Tevara sthalams of the Pandya country and one of the 275 Paadal Petra Sthalams, with royal patronage running from the early Cholas and Pandyas to the Sethupathis and Marudu Pandiyars.
story: At Mahalakshmi's request, Shiva is said to have revealed his Gowri Thandavam cosmic dance to her at this shrine.

name: Vruddhapureeswarar Temple, Thiruppunavayil
significance: A coastal-country shrine of Pudukkottai district counted as the seventh of the Pandya-region Tevara sthalams, where Sambandar, Appar and Sundarar each sang the presiding deity.
story: The four Vedas together with Brahma, Vishnu and Lakshmi, Indra, Surya, Chandra and the sages Vasishta and Agastya are all said to have worshipped Shiva here.

name: Adhi Ratneswarar Temple
deity: Shiva as Adhi Ratneswarar, with Snehavalli
significance: A major shrine of Ramanathapuram district, one of the fourteen Tevaram-praised Shiva temples of the Pandya country and of the 275 Paadal Petra Sthalams, its gopuram carrying fine Dravidian work.
story: Vaaruni, cursed to bear an elephant's body with a goat's head, is said to have regained his form by worshipping Shiva here, giving Tiruvadanai its name.

name: Sornakaleeswarar (Kaleeswarar) Temple, Kalaiyarkoil
deity: Shiva as Kaleeswarar (Sornakaleeswarar), with Parvati as Swarnambikai
builtDisplay: present temple c. 700 years old; Tevaram-era origins
significance: The great temple of Kalaiyarkoil, ancient Thirukkaanapper, with a 150-foot rajagopuram and three linked Shiva shrines; Sundarar sang its deity, placing it among the Paadal Petra Sthalams. The Marudu brothers of Sivaganga later fortified the site.
story: The goddess Kali is said to have worshipped the Kaleeswarar linga here before defeating the demon Chandasura with the seven mothers.

name: Pushpavaneswarar Temple, Tiruppuvanam
deity: Shiva as Pushpavaneswarar, with Parvati as Soundaranayagi
builtDisplay: 7th c. origins; stone temple by Aditya Chola I (870-907)
significance: A Vaigai-bank temple of the Pandya country revered in the Tevaram, its stone structure raised under Aditya I with further Chola endowments from Uttama Chola to Rajendra I recorded in inscriptions.
story: A devoted dancer named Ponanaial is said to have been divinely helped to fashion a golden Shiva idol, on which her pinch-marks remain visible.

name: Thirumeninathar Temple, Thiruchuli
deity: Shiva as Thirumeninathar, with Parvati as Thunaimalaiyammai
significance: The Paadal Petra Sthalam of Thiruchuli in Virudhunagar district, a Pandya foundation built on the plan of the great Madurai and Rameswaram temples and closely associated with the saint Sundarar.
story: During the great deluge Shiva is said to have swallowed the floodwaters here in a swirl ('chuli'), giving the town its name.

name: Kutralanathar Temple, Courtallam
deity: Shiva as Kutralanathar, with Parvati as Kuzhalvaimozhi Ammai
significance: The temple of Courtallam by its famous waterfalls, laid out on a conch-shaped plan and housing the Chitra Sabha, one of the five cosmic dance halls of Nataraja; Sambandar's Tevaram places it among the Paadal Petra Sthalams.
story: Sage Agastya, unable to attend Shiva's wedding in the north, prayed here and was granted a vision of the lord in full marriage attire.

name: Nellaiappar Temple
deity: Shiva as Nellaiappar (Venuvananathar), with Parvati as Kanthimathi Amman
builtDisplay: 7th c. core (Pandya); walls, halls and gardens added 13th-18th c.
significance: The vast twin temple of Nellaiappar and Kanthimathi dominating Tirunelveli, its sanctums credited to the 7th-century Pandya Nindraseer Nedumaran, with musical pillars and later mandapams spread over nearly six hectares. It is a Paadal Petra Sthalam of the Tevaram canon.
story: Vishnu is said to have witnessed the wedding of Shiva and Parvati in the bamboo grove (Venuvana) that gave the deity his name.

name: Avinashiappar Temple (Tiruppukkozhiyur)
deity: Shiva as Avinashiappar (Avinasilingeswarar), with Parvati as Karunambigai
significance: The chief Tevaram shrine of the Kongu country at Avinashi, founded under the Cholas and rebuilt in stone under the Nayaks, counted among the 275 Paadal Petra Sthalams.
story: At Sundarar's hymn, a crocodile is said to have released alive the boy it had swallowed years before, an event replayed each year as the Mudalai Vaai Pillai festival.

name: Thirumuruganatheeswarar Temple
deity: Shiva as Thirumuruganatheeswarar, with Parvati as Avudainayagi
significance: A 10th-century Kongu Chola temple near Tiruppur, its walls carrying 68 inscriptions of Vikrama Chola, revered in the Tevaram and classed as a garden temple (Kokkudi Koil) among the Paadal Petra Sthalams.
story: Murugan is said to have worshipped his father here to shed the sin of slaying Surapadma, digging a spring with his vel to purify himself.

name: Sangameswarar Temple, Bhavani
significance: The confluence temple where the Bhavani meets the Kaveri, known in the Tevaram as Thirunana; Sambandar dedicated ten hymns of the second Thirumurai to its deity, and Arunagirinathar later sang its Subramanya.
story: Kubera, flying overhead, is said to have seen a deer, tiger, cow, elephant, snake and rat drinking together beneath an ilandhai tree, revealing the sanctity of the confluence.

name: Ardhanareeswarar Temple, Tiruchengode
deity: Ardhanarishvara, the composite form of Shiva and Parvati
significance: The hill temple of Tiruchengode enshrining Ardhanarishvara, the half-male half-female form of Shiva and Parvati, among the 275 Paadal Petra Sthalams; Krishnadevaraya raised its Thirumalai gopuram in 1512, and an emerald lingam is among its treasures.
story: When the sage Bhringi circumambulated only Shiva, Parvati performed austerities until the two merged into the single body of Ardhanareeswarar.

name: Vikirtheeswarar Temple, Venjamakoodal
significance: The Paadal Petra Sthalam of the Kongu country at Venjamangudalur in Karur district, over twelve centuries old with rock inscriptions of the Pandya period; Sundarar composed a Tevaram pathigam here.
story: Shiva, in the guise of a priest, is said to have blessed Sundarar with gold at this shrine first raised by the hunter-king Venchan.

name: Magudeswarar Temple, Kodumudi
deity: Shiva as Magudeswarar (Kodumudi Nathar), with Parvati as Panmozhi Nayaki
significance: The sixth Tevaram shrine of the Kongu country, on the Kaveri at Kodumudi, sung by Sambandar, Appar and Sundarar alike and bearing epigraphs of Pandya rulers including Maravarman Sundarapandian.
story: A crow is said to have tipped over sage Agastya's water-pot here, the spilt water flowing on as the Kaveri to nourish the farmlands downstream.

name: Pasupateeswarar Temple, Karur
deity: Shiva as Pasupateeswarar (Aanilaiappar), with Sundaravalli and Alankaravalli
builtDisplay: by 7th c. (Tevaram era); Chola land grants from Rajendra I
significance: The ancient temple of Karuvoor Aanilai in Karur town, a Paadal Petra Sthalam where Sambandar and Sundarar sang, later endowed by Rajendra Chola and patronised by Kongu Chola, Kongu Pandya and Vijayanagara rulers. Its swayambu lingam stands behind a 120-foot gopuram.
story: The celestial cow Kamadhenu is said to have worshipped the lingam here, and Brahma's worship gave the tank its name Brahma Theertham.

name: Theerthapurisvarar Temple, Tiruvattatthurai
significance: The village shrine of ancient Tirunelvayil Aratturai in Cuddalore district, a Paadal Petra Sthalam where Sambandar, Appar and Sundarar are all held to have worshipped.

name: Sudarkozhundeeswarar Temple, Pennadam
significance: An early Chola temple at Pennadam whose apsidal sanctum is shaped like an elephant's back (gajaprishthakara), counted among the 275 Paadal Petra Sthalams and visited by the saint Appar on his pilgrimages.

name: Narthana Vallabeswarar Temple
deity: Shiva as Narthana Vallabeswarar, with Parvati as Gnanasakthi
significance: A river-confluence shrine of Cuddalore district founded under the Cholas and rebuilt in the Nayak period, glorified by Sundarar among the Paadal Petra Sthalams.
story: A Chola king who had wrongfully killed his wife is said to have been cured of the resulting affliction by bathing at the confluence where Shiva rules as Koodalaiyitroorar.

name: Thirukumaresar (Neelakandeswarar) Temple
deity: Shiva as Thirukumaresar (Thiruneelakandeswarar), with Parvati as Verumulai Amman
significance: The Paadal Petra Sthalam of ancient Erukkattampuliyur, birthplace of Tirunilakanta Nayanar of the 63 Nayanmars; the Chola foundation was rebuilt under the Nayaks behind a five-tiered gopuram.
story: Raja Raja Chola is said to have prayed here and been blessed with his son Rajendra, after whom the village was renamed Rajendirapattinam.

name: Veerateeswarar Temple, Thiruvathigai
deity: Shiva as Veerattaaneswarar, with Parvati as Thiripurasundari
significance: One of the eight Veeratta shrines of Shiva, marking his destruction of the three demon cities; here the Pallava king Mahendravarman I embraced Saivism, and the saint Appar returned to the faith and attained salvation. Its seven-tiered gopuram carries early Bharatanatyam sculpture.
story: Shiva is said to have burnt the three flying cities of the asuras from this spot, with Vishnu himself serving as the arrow.

name: Bhaktajaneswarar Temple, Thirunavalur
deity: Shiva as Bhaktajaneswarar, with Parvati as Manonmani Amman
builtDisplay: 16th c. masonry; Chola origins with Parantaka I inscriptions
significance: The temple of Thirunavalur, home village of the saint-poet Sundarar, with inscriptions running from Parantaka I to Rajendra Chola III; it stands among the 275 Paadal Petra Sthalams of the Tevaram canon.
story: The shrine's sacred naval tree is traced in legend to a drop spilt during the churning of the ocean of milk.

name: Vriddhagiriswarar Temple, Vriddhachalam
deity: Shiva as Vriddhagiriswarar (Pazhamalai Nadhar), with Viruthambigai (Periyanayaki)
significance: The great temple of Tirumudukunram ('the old hill'), commissioned by the Chola queen Sembiyan Mahadevi, with five gopurams and a chariot-shaped hundred-pillared hall. A Paadal Petra Sthalam held to grant salvation to departed souls even beyond Varanasi's power.
story: Shiva is said to have taken the form of an ancient mountain at Brahma's prayer, earning the name Pazhamalai, the old hill.

name: Atulya Nadheswarar Temple
deity: Shiva as Atulya Nadheswarar, with Parvati as Azhagiya Ponnazhagi
significance: A hill temple above the Thenpennai at Arakandanallur, grown from three Pallava rock-cut caves through Chola expansion to its 16th-century Vijayanagara form, and sung by Sambandar among the Paadal Petra Sthalams. Ramana Maharshi is believed to have stayed in its caves before being drawn to Tiruvannamalai.
story: Vishnu is said to have prayed to Shiva here to be cleansed after subduing Mahabali in his Vamana avatar.

name: Marudeeswarar Temple, T. Edaiyar
deity: Shiva as Marudeeswarar (Idayatrunathar), with Parvati as Gnanambigai
builtDisplay: 16th c. masonry; Chola origins with Rajaraja I inscriptions
significance: A Thenpennai-bank shrine of Viluppuram district revered in the Tevaram of Sambandar and Sundarar, its Chola core recorded in inscriptions of Rajaraja I, Kulothunga I and Rajendra III before a 16th-century rebuilding.
story: The sage who overheard Shiva's secret teaching to Parvati was cursed and, reborn as Vyasa, is said to have won redemption by worshipping here.

name: Kripapureeswarar Temple, Thiruvennainallur
deity: Shiva as Kripapureeswarar (Arutkondanathar), with Parvati as Mangalambigai
builtDisplay: 10th c. (Chola); Sembiyan Mahadevi and Rajaraja I endowments
significance: The 10th-century Chola temple where the saint-poet Sundarar, claimed by Shiva as his slave, began the Tirumurai; it was endowed by queen Sembiyan Mahadevi and Rajaraja I and stands among the Paadal Petra Sthalams.
story: Shiva, appearing as an old man with a palm-leaf bond over Sundarar, revealed himself and bade the saint sing, beginning with the word 'Pitha' - the first verse of the Tevaram.

name: Sishtagurunatheswarar Temple, Tirutturaiyur
significance: A village shrine of Cuddalore district counted among the 275 Paadal Petra Sthalams, glorified in the early medieval Tevaram hymns of the saint Appar.

name: Vadukeeswarar Temple, Thiruvandarkoil
deity: Shiva as Vadukeeswarar, with Parvati as Thiripura Sundari
builtDisplay: 16th c. masonry; Chola-era origins with Parantaka I inscriptions
significance: The Paadal Petra Sthalam of ancient Thiru Vadukur, now Thiruvandarkoil in Puducherry, its Chola core attested by inscriptions of Parantaka I, Rajaraja I, Kulothunga I and Rajendra III beneath a 16th-century rebuilding.
story: The name Vadukeeswarar - 'he who quivered' - recalls Shiva's severing of the fifth head of a prideful Brahma.
